instruction:
Update section '## 5. Use filters to focus' in 'apps/docs/core/functional/plan-and-execute-tasks.mdx' to describe the board filter chip anatomy and clearing behavior in detail while preserving the existing five-filter list. Ensure the documentation reflects the following factual contract:

1. Active Filter Chips (FR-1):
- Active filters render as removable ActiveFilterChip components in the board toolbar next to the Filter dropdown and Sort control.
- Each chip contains divider-separated sections: Subject, Operator, Value, and a Clear button (X).

2. Chip Behaviors & Display Asymmetry (FR-2):
- Status: subject 'Status', operator 'is any of', stacked status icons (up to 3), value displays column name if exactly 1 is selected, otherwise '{count} selected'.
- Priority: subject 'Priority', operator 'is any of', stacked priority icons (up to 3), value displays priority label if exactly 1 is selected, otherwise '{count} selected'.
- Assignee: subject 'Assignee', operator 'is any of', stacked avatars (up to 3), value displays user name if exactly 1 is selected, otherwise '{count} selected'.
- Due date: subject 'Due date', operator 'is any of', no stacked icons, value displays 'Due this week', 'Due next week', or 'No due date' if exactly 1 is selected, otherwise '{count} selected'.
- Labels: subject 'Labels', operator 'include any of' (note operator difference from 'is any of'), value is ALWAYS '{count} selected' (there is no single-label naming branch; it always displays a count).

3. Filter Clearing (FR-3):
- Clicking the Clear button (X) on an individual chip resets only that specific filter criterion without affecting others.
- 'Clear all filters' is a menu item located INSIDE the Filter dropdown menu (shown only when at least one filter is active); it is not a standalone toolbar button.

4. Constraints (NFR-1, NFR-3):
- Match repo .mdx house style.
- Keep frontmatter and sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and Next untouched.
- Do not modify any other file.
acceptance: Section '## 5. Use filters to focus' accurately documents ActiveFilterChip placement, chip anatomy (Subject, Operator, Value, Clear X), and clearing mechanics.
The documentation details all 5 filter types with exact operators ('is any of' for Status, Priority, Assignee, Due date; 'include any of' for Labels).

The documentation explicitly notes that Status, Priority, Assignee, and Due date display named values when exactly 1 option is selected vs '{count} selected' when multiple are selected, while Labels always displays '{count} selected' with no single-label naming branch.
The documentation notes stacked icons (max 3) for Status, Priority, Assignee, and no icons for Due date.
The documentation states that 'Clear all filters' resides inside the Filter dropdown menu (when active filters exist), not as a standalone toolbar button.
The five-filter bullet list (- Status, - Priority, - Assignee, - Due date, - Labels) is preserved.
Frontmatter and sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, Next remain untouched.
_planning_notes: A single TaskPacket is planned because the scope is strictly confined to rewriting section 5 within one file. The write allowlist contains only this file; splitting a single section update across packets would add complexity without benefit.
